rules.title: Los Angeles RSO allowable annual rent increase
rules.requirement: For RSO units, rent may be raised only once every 12 months by the LAHD-published allowable percentage. Effective February 2, 2026, landlords may no longer add an extra percentage for utilities. Larger increases require LAHD approval (capital improvement, primary renovation, seismic retrofit, rehabilitation, just and reasonable). Rent may reset to market after a voluntary move-out or certain evictions.
rules.key_value: Once every 12 months by LAHD allowable rent increase percentage; no added utility percentage as of 2026-02-02
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental properties in the City of Los Angeles first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28. Covered types include apartments, condos, townhomes, duplexes, two or more single-family dwellings on one parcel, hotel or motel rooms occupied over 30 days, units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs, JADUs, and mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Rent amount is not regulated for condo or townhome tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995. Luxury exemption is available by application. Temporary exemptions may apply.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Replacement units under LAMC 151.28 are covered regardless of age. A single-family dwelling alone on a parcel is generally not covered (only two or more per parcel). Condo/townhome rent is not regulated for tenancies commenced after 1995-12-31. Luxury and temporary exemptions apply.

rules.citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (LAMC Ch. XV, § 151.00 et seq.)
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO additional-tenant rent increase; dependent increase eliminated
rules.requirement: Effective February 2, 2026, landlords may not add a 10% increase for an additional dependent. A 10% increase is still allowed for an additional non-dependent tenant, imposed within 60 days of the landlord learning of that tenant.
rules.key_value: 10% for additional (non-dependent) tenant; 0% for dependents as of 2026-02-02
rules.coverage_conditions: RSO units in the City of Los Angeles (first built on or before October 1, 1978).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Depends on whether the added occupant is a dependent and when the landlord learned of the occupant.

rules.citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (LAMC Ch. XV, § 151.00 et seq.)
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO legal reasons for eviction
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO units may evict only for listed at-fault reasons or listed no-fault reasons. At-fault reasons include nonpayment, lease violation, nuisance or damage, illegal use, refusal to renew a similar agreement, denial of access, and an unapproved subtenant. No-fault reasons include owner or family move-in, resident manager, demolition or removal from the rental market, government order, and conversion to affordable housing.
rules.coverage_conditions: RSO units in the City of Los Angeles (first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units).

rules.title: Filing of termination notices with LAHD
rules.requirement: Every notice terminating a tenancy of an RSO unit must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service on the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the RSO in the City of Los Angeles (the cited LAMC 165.05.B.5 also covers Just Cause Ordinance units).

rules.title: Relocation assistance and notice for no-fault evictions under RSO
rules.requirement: No-fault evictions of RSO tenants require filing a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD. The landlord must give 30- or 60-day written notice (some require 120 days or up to a 1-year extension) and pay tenant relocation assistance.
rules.coverage_conditions: RSO units in the City of Los Angeles.

rules.title: Notice of Right to Counsel
rules.requirement: Beginning August 20, 2025, landlords must post the Notice of Right to Counsel and give it to the tenant at the start of the tenancy. The notice must also be attached to any eviction notice or rental subsidy termination.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of rental units in the City of Los Angeles (described on the RSO page).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Page does not state whether the requirement is limited to RSO units.
